meta.description: Seed timeline of defendant- and regulator-origin language relevant to compulsive-use design and boundary erosion analysis. This is a structured evidence index, not an adjudication of liability.

events.actor: Meta (internal, as reported in WA AG statement)
events.signal_text: Internal communications described notification practices as overused and discussed reduction proposals tied to problematic use.

events.actor: Meta (internal, as reported in WA AG statement)
events.signal_text: Internal proposal to leadership referenced scientific evidence that average net wellbeing effects were slightly negative.

events.actor: Meta congressional testimony (as quoted in filed complaint)
events.signal_text: Public denial that platforms were built to be addictive, contrasted with allegations of design features that impede disengagement.
Complaint frames recommendation systems, likes/social comparison, notifications, autoplay, and infinite scroll as compulsive-use architecture.

events.actor: Plaintiffs filing in MDL 3047 citing internal communications
events.signal_text: Filed brief cites internal chat language comparing platform dynamics to drug-pusher dynamics and reward-deficit framing.
Commission preliminarily found addictive design concerns tied to infinite scroll, autoplay, push notifications, and recommender dynamics.
Order denying motion to dismiss summarizes allegations around recommendation systems, infinite scroll, autoplay, likes/comments, and push notifications.
